stem: A maternity unit uses a newborn security plan that includes parent-infant identification checks and other safeguards. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Rely on the electronic security device alone and omit identification checks that the unit security plan requires.
options.B: Perform identification verification only when a staff member suspects a security problem rather than as required by the established plan.
options.C: Follow the established newborn security plan, including all required parent-infant identification checks and safeguards.
options.D: Suspend routine newborn security procedures when the unit has had no recent incidents because security plans apply only after a documented threat.

rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly includes following security plans and procedures, with newborn security given as an example, under Safety and Infection Prevention and Control. Because the scenario states that the unit's established plan requires identification checks and other safeguards, the nurse should follow those required components rather than omit them based on an electronic control, personal suspicion, or absence of recent incidents. C is correct.
educational_objective: Follow the facility's established newborn security plan and complete its required identification and safety procedures consistently.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: 'Follow security plan and procedures (e.g., newborn security...)' and protect clients/healthcare personnel from health and environmental hazards.
source_claim_supported: Nurses should follow established security plans and procedures, including newborn-security procedures; required plan components should not be selectively omitted.

source_original.stem: A maternity unit uses a newborn security plan that includes parent-infant identification checks and other safeguards. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Rely on the electronic security device after activation because required parent-infant identification verification then becomes redundant.
options.B: Perform identification verification only when a staff member suspects a security problem rather than as required by the established plan.
options.C: Follow all applicable components of the newborn security plan, including required identification verification; one electronic control does not replace staff checks.
options.D: Suspend routine newborn security procedures when the unit has had no recent incidents because security plans apply only after a documented threat.

source_original.rationale: The current NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly includes following security plans and procedures, including newborn security, within Safety and Infection Prevention and Control. Layered facility procedures must be followed rather than substituting one control for the plan.
source_original.source_detail: Overview of Content — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: “Follow security plan and procedures (e.g., newborn security...)”. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: infection prevention, biohazard handling, security plans, equipment safety and workplace safety. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the security-plan construct and key C, removed an unnecessarily broad 'layered controls' claim and anchored the answer solely to following the established plan described in the stem and explicitly represented in NCSBN. Difficulty reduced from hard to medium.

audit_findings.exact_locator: Printed p.8 Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, rendered screenshot verified
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item now tests only the directly supported requirement to follow the established security plan, including the plan components stated in the stem.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because it instructs omission of a required plan component.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because required plan procedures are not conditional on individual suspicion.
distractor_audit.C: Correct and directly aligned with NCSBN.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because established security procedures are not suspended merely because recent incidents are absent.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C follows the stated plan without inventing an exception.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives concern compliance with the same established newborn-security plan.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — follow security plan/procedures.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the official NCSBN p.8 screenshot, stem, all options, rationale and objective. C remained uniquely correct without relying on unsupported facility-specific assumptions.
